title: Layer connectivity: fighting over-smoothing
blurb: Expressive layers, MLP pre/post layers, skip connections

hook.title: Keep the early drafts
hook.text: You revise an essay through many drafts. The more you rewrite, the blurrier your original voice. Smart writers keep the early drafts alongside the latest: the final piece is a mix of lightly revised and heavily revised versions. A **skip connection** does that for a GNN: the final embedding includes the *earlier-layer* embeddings, which still distinguish nodes, and effectively gives you an ensemble of shallow and deep GNNs.
hook.recall: Remember keeping the early drafts: skip connections add the earlier embedding back ($F(x)+x$), and $N$ skips make $2^N$ paths, a mixture of shallow and deep GNNs.

explore.intro: 12-node graph in two communities. Add layers with and without skip connections.
tasks: With a plain stack go from 0 to 12 layers. What happens to the spread and to the distance between nodes from different communities?
Switch on skip connections and repeat.
explore.takeaway: Shallow GNNs can be made more expressive by (1) deeper aggregation/transformation inside layers, (2) MLP pre/post-process layers, (3) skip connections for when many layers are really needed.

build.prompt: Write the GCN layer with a skip connection (slide 22).

questions.prompt: **Solution 1** for making a *shallow* GNN more expressive:
options: Increase the expressive power within each GNN layer (e.g. make aggregation/transformation a deep network)
questions.explanation: Each aggregation/transformation can be more than one linear layer.

options: Add MLP layers (applied to each node) before and after the GNN layers (pre-/post-process layers)
questions.explanation: A GNN doesn’t only have to contain GNN layers.

questions.prompt: $N=4$ skip connections create how many possible paths (a mixture of shallow and deep GNNs)?
Which statement about skip connections is FALSE?
options: They create a mixture of shallow and deep GNNs
Node embeddings in earlier layers can sometimes better differentiate nodes
They make a GNN strictly shallower
questions.explanation: They don’t reduce depth; they add shortcut paths from earlier layers.

questions.prompt: Why do earlier-layer embeddings help against over-smoothing?
options: They can sometimes better differentiate nodes
questions.explanation: The early drafts still carry the original voice.

questions.prompt: *“Once I add skip connections the number of layers doesn’t matter at all; use $L=100$.”* What’s wrong?
options: Slide 17 still warns not to set $L$ unnecessarily large; skip connections *help*, they don’t make depth free
questions.explanation: Better editors still don’t need 100 drafts.
